full_judgment:
3. The case of the plaintiff is that the suit land appertaining to C.S. Khatian No. 1 of Mouza Darigachha under P.S. and District-Bogra originally belonged to landlord Bimalendu Roy Bahadur. During C.S. operation, the land was recorded in C.S. Khatian No. 1 in his name. But in the remarks column of the Khatian the suit land was written as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” Actually, the local people had no possession in, or prescriptive right over the suit land as such, the recital “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” in the remarks column of the C.S. Khatian was wrong and illegal. 

 7. Defendant Nos. 13 and 14 filed another written statement. Their case is that the land of plot No. 794 is a tank and that plot No. 2446 measuring 7.07 is a part of River Bhadai, used by the local people. Since there is no embankment of the tank, the local people use the water of the tank for irrigation from the time of their forefathers. Accordingly, in the remarks column of the C.S  khatian, the suit land was shown “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” By practicing fraud upon the local authority and suppressing the rec9rd containing the entry “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” the plaintiff took settlement of the suit land. 

 15. Having perused C.S. khatian No. 1 of Mouza Darigacha, I find that plot No. 794 was shown as tank and in its remarks column, the tank was shown as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয” Chapter 111 of the Government State Manual, 1958 gives detailed descriptions of the Register that is to be maintained. According to Rule 22, Register VIII is a register of unoccupied lands and will be maintained in parts: 

 16. From the above rule, it appears that water tanks used by public cannot be leased out. In the case in hand, we find that in violation of the above rule, the land of plot No. 794 was leased out to the plaintiff. It is, however, contended that in the remarks column of C.S. record through mistake it was written “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. In this connection, it is important to note here that according to section 103 B (5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act, every entry made in a record-of-rights shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. The plaintiff, how-ever, could not rebut the presumption of correctness of the entry made in the C.S. khatian including the entry made in its remarks column in which it was written “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. 

 In the present case the land was recorded in the C.S. record as well as S.A. Khatian as “সর্ব সাধারণের ব্যবহারয”. As the public had rights in the disputed land, the settlement made in favour of the plaintiff was not legally done, and by the impugned orders such settlement was correctly cancelled by the revenue authorities."
